subproblems.title: Single-scale change-of-variables identities for the blown-up Hausdorff measure
subproblems.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ, Hⁿ = μHE[n], ω_n = unitBallVolume n and V(r) := ω_n·ofReal(rⁿ) ∈ [0,∞] for r ∈ ℝ; ‖·‖ₑ is the [0,∞]-valued operator norm on MultiVector P n = Λ_n(ℝ^P), B̄ = closedBall, B = ball, and products and quotients are taken in [0,∞]. Let M ⊆ ℝ^P (= Euclid P) be an arbitrary set, θ : ℝ^P → ℝ and ζ : ℝ^P → MultiVector P n arbitrary functions, a ∈ ℝ^P and λ > 0. Put N := blowUpMap a λ '' M = {λ⁻¹(x − a) : x ∈ M}, ν := Hⁿ⌞N (μHE[n].restrict N), D := dilation a λ (the contract's map y ↦ −λ⁻¹a + λ⁻¹y) and c := ofReal(λ⁻¹ ^ n). Assume (H) ν = c·D_#(Hⁿ⌞M), i.e. μHE[n].restrict N = ENNReal.ofReal (λ⁻¹ ^ n) • Measure.map D (μHE[n].restrict M). Then (i) ν(ℝ^P) = c·Hⁿ(M); and for every R > 0: (ii) ν(B̄_R(0)) = V(R)·(Hⁿ(M ∩ B̄_{λR}(a))/V(λR)); (iii) ν(B_R(0)) = V(R)·(Hⁿ(M ∩ B_{λR}(a))/V(λR)); (iv) ∫⁻_{B̄_R(0)} ‖θ(a + λy)ζ(a + λy) − θ(a)ζ(a)‖ₑ dν(y) = V(R)·((∫⁻_{M ∩ B̄_{λR}(a)} ‖θ(x)ζ(x) − θ(a)ζ(a)‖ₑ dHⁿ(x))/V(λR)).
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (M : Set (Euclid P)) (θ : Euclid P → ℝ) (ζ : Euclid P → MultiVector P n) (a : Euclid P) (lam : ℝ), 0 < lam → μHE[n].restrict (Poincare.SimonGMT.Chapter03.blowUpMap a lam '' M) = ENNReal.ofReal (lam⁻¹ ^ n) • Measure.map (dilation a lam) (μHE[n].restrict M) → (μHE[n].restrict (Poincare.SimonGMT.Chapter03.blowUpMap a lam '' M)) univ = ENNReal.ofReal (lam⁻¹ ^ n) * μHE[n] M ∧ ∀ R : ℝ, 0 < R → (μHE[n].restrict (Poincare.SimonGMT.Chapter03.blowUpMap a lam '' M)) (closedBall 0 R) = unitBallVolume n * ENNReal.ofReal (R ^ n) * (μHE[n] (M ∩ closedBall a (lam * R)) / (unitBallVolume n * ENNReal.ofReal ((lam * R) ^ n))) ∧ (μHE[n].restrict (Poincare.SimonGMT.Chapter03.blowUpMap a lam '' M)) (ball 0 R) = unitBallVolume n * ENNReal.ofReal (R ^ n) * (μHE[n] (M ∩ ball a (lam * R)) / (unitBallVolume n * ENNReal.ofReal ((lam * R) ^ n))) ∧ ∫⁻ y in closedBall (0 : Euclid P) R, ‖θ (a + lam • y) • ζ (a + lam • y) - θ a • ζ a‖ₑ ∂(μHE[n].restrict (Poincare.SimonGMT.Chapter03.blowUpMap a lam '' M)) = unitBallVolume n * ENNReal.ofReal (R ^ n) * ((∫⁻ x in M ∩ closedBall a (lam * R), ‖θ x • ζ x - θ a • ζ a‖ₑ ∂μHE[n]) / (unitBallVolume n * ENNReal.ofReal ((lam * R) ^ n)))
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: steps 1–2 of the parent proof (change of variables; balls and constants), specialised to a single scale λ. The parent obtains ν_i = c_i·(D_i)_#(Hⁿ⌞M) from the sibling blowup_measure, part (ii); here that identity is the hypothesis (H), which the parent supplies when it applies this lemma with λ = λ_i. Notation is as in the statement; all measures are on the Borel σ-algebra of ℝ^P.
1. (D is a homeomorphism; inverse formula.) By definition dilationCLM P λ = λ⁻¹·id, so D(y) = −(λ⁻¹a) + λ⁻¹y = λ⁻¹(y − a) for every y. Since λ⁻¹ ≠ 0, D is the composition of the homeomorphism y ↦ λ⁻¹y (Homeomorph.smulOfNeZero λ⁻¹) with the translation z ↦ −(λ⁻¹a) + z (Homeomorph.addLeft). Hence D is a homeomorphism of ℝ^P, and in particular a measurable embedding (Homeomorph.measurableEmbedding). Moreover a + λ·D(x) = a + λλ⁻¹(x − a) = x for every x ∈ ℝ^P.
2. (Preimages of balls.) For y ∈ ℝ^P, ‖D(y)‖ = ‖λ⁻¹(y − a)‖ = λ⁻¹‖y − a‖ = λ⁻¹·dist(y, a), because λ > 0. Hence, for every R ∈ ℝ: D(y) ∈ B̄_R(0) ⇔ λ⁻¹·dist(y, a) ≤ R ⇔ dist(y, a) ≤ λR (inv_mul_le_iff₀), i.e. D⁻¹(B̄_R(0)) = B̄_{λR}(a); and with strict inequalities (inv_mul_lt_iff₀), D⁻¹(B_R(0)) = B_{λR}(a). These preimages are closed, resp. open, hence Borel.
3. (Masses of sets.) Let S ⊆ ℝ^P with D⁻¹(S) Borel. By (H) and the definition of a scalar multiple of a measure, ν(S) = c·(D_#(Hⁿ⌞M))(S) (Measure.smul_apply). Since D is a measurable embedding, (D_#(Hⁿ⌞M))(S) = (Hⁿ⌞M)(D⁻¹(S)) (MeasurableEmbedding.map_apply), and since D⁻¹(S) is measurable, (Hⁿ⌞M)(D⁻¹(S)) = Hⁿ(D⁻¹(S) ∩ M) (Measure.restrict_apply). Thus ν(S) = c·Hⁿ(M ∩ D⁻¹(S)).
4. (The normalising constant.) ω_n is the Lebesgue measure of the open unit ball of ℝⁿ, so ω_n > 0 (a nonempty open ball has positive measure, measure_ball_pos) and ω_n < ∞ (balls have finite Lebesgue measure, measure_ball_lt_top). Fix R > 0. Then λR > 0, so (λR)ⁿ > 0 and V(λR) = ω_n·ofReal((λR)ⁿ) ∈ (0, ∞). Cancelling the common factor ω_n ∈ (0, ∞) (ENNReal.mul_div_mul_left) and using ofReal(x)/ofReal(y) = ofReal(x/y) for y > 0 (ENNReal.ofReal_div_of_pos), V(R)/V(λR) = ofReal(Rⁿ)/ofReal((λR)ⁿ) = ofReal(Rⁿ/(λR)ⁿ) = ofReal(Rⁿ/(λⁿRⁿ)) = ofReal((λ⁻¹)ⁿ) = c, where Rⁿ ≠ 0 and λ ≠ 0 were used. Consequently, for every X ∈ [0, ∞], writing u/v = u·v⁻¹ in [0, ∞] and using associativity and commutativity of multiplication, c·X = (V(R)·V(λR)⁻¹)·X = V(R)·(X·V(λR)⁻¹) = V(R)·(X/V(λR)).
5. (Conclusion (i).) Take S = ℝ^P in step 3 (D⁻¹(ℝ^P) = ℝ^P is Borel): ν(ℝ^P) = c·Hⁿ(M ∩ ℝ^P) = c·Hⁿ(M).
6. (Conclusions (ii) and (iii).) Let R > 0. By steps 2 and 3 with S = B̄_R(0), resp. S = B_R(0): ν(B̄_R(0)) = c·Hⁿ(M ∩ B̄_{λR}(a)) and ν(B_R(0)) = c·Hⁿ(M ∩ B_{λR}(a)). Step 4 with X = Hⁿ(M ∩ B̄_{λR}(a)), resp. X = Hⁿ(M ∩ B_{λR}(a)), gives (ii) and (iii).
7. (Conclusion (iv).) Let R > 0, S := B̄_R(0) and g(y) := ‖θ(a + λy)ζ(a + λy) − θ(a)ζ(a)‖ₑ ∈ [0, ∞]. By (H), ν⌞S = c·((D_#(Hⁿ⌞M))⌞S) (restriction commutes with scalar multiplication, Measure.restrict_smul), so ∫⁻_S g dν = c·∫⁻ g d((D_#(Hⁿ⌞M))⌞S) (lintegral_smul_measure). As D is a measurable embedding, (D_#(Hⁿ⌞M))⌞S = D_#((Hⁿ⌞M)⌞D⁻¹(S)) (MeasurableEmbedding.restrict_map), and ∫⁻ g d(D_#ρ) = ∫⁻ (g∘D) dρ for every measure ρ and every g : ℝ^P → [0, ∞] (MeasurableEmbedding.lintegral_map; no measurability of g is needed). Since D⁻¹(S) = B̄_{λR}(a) is Borel (step 2), (Hⁿ⌞M)⌞D⁻¹(S) = Hⁿ⌞(D⁻¹(S) ∩ M) = Hⁿ⌞(M ∩ B̄_{λR}(a)) (Measure.restrict_restrict). Finally, by step 1, g(D(x)) = ‖θ(a + λD(x))ζ(a + λD(x)) − θ(a)ζ(a)‖ₑ = ‖θ(x)ζ(x) − θ(a)ζ(a)‖ₑ for every x. Hence ∫⁻_S g dν = c·∫⁻_{M ∩ B̄_{λR}(a)} ‖θ(x)ζ(x) − θ(a)ζ(a)‖ₑ dHⁿ(x), and step 4 applied to X equal to this last integral gives (iv). ∎
proof_key_steps: D = dilation a λ is y ↦ λ⁻¹(y − a), a homeomorphism (Homeomorph.smulOfNeZero followed by Homeomorph.addLeft), hence a measurable embedding, and a + λ·D(x) = x.
‖D(y)‖ = λ⁻¹·dist(y, a), so D⁻¹(B̄_R(0)) = B̄_{λR}(a) and D⁻¹(B_R(0)) = B_{λR}(a).
From (H): ν(S) = c·Hⁿ(M ∩ D⁻¹S) whenever D⁻¹S is Borel, and ∫⁻_S g dν = c·∫⁻_{M ∩ D⁻¹S} g∘D dHⁿ (restrict_smul, lintegral_smul_measure, restrict_map, lintegral_map, restrict_restrict).
0 < ω_n < ∞ gives c = V(R)/V(λR) for R > 0, hence c·X = V(R)·(X/V(λR)) for all X ∈ [0,∞].
Apply with S = ℝ^P, B̄_R(0), B_R(0) and with g(y) = ‖θ(a + λy)ζ(a + λy) − θ(a)ζ(a)‖ₑ, using g∘D = ‖θζ − θ(a)ζ(a)‖ₑ, to obtain (i)–(iv).

subproblems.title: Transfer of one-sided limits at 0⁺ to a positive null sequence with a finite constant factor
subproblems.statement: Let f, h : ℝ → [0,∞], let C ∈ [0,∞] with C ≠ ∞, and let s : ℕ → ℝ satisfy s_i > 0 for every i and s_i → 0 as i → ∞. Then (i) if limsup_{r→0⁺} f(r) ≤ 1 (limsup along 𝓝[>] 0), then limsup_{i→∞} C·f(s_i) ≤ C; and (ii) if h(r) → 0 as r → 0⁺ (along 𝓝[>] 0), then C·h(s_i) → 0 as i → ∞.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (f h : ℝ → ℝ≥0∞) (C : ℝ≥0∞) (s : ℕ → ℝ), C ≠ ∞ → (∀ i, 0 < s i) → Tendsto s atTop (𝓝 0) → (limsup f (𝓝[>] 0) ≤ 1 → limsup (fun i => C * f (s i)) atTop ≤ C) ∧ (Tendsto h (𝓝[>] 0) (𝓝 0) → Tendsto (fun i => C * h (s i)) atTop (𝓝 0))
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: the limit arguments of steps 5 and 7 of the parent proof (composition with λ_iR → 0 in 𝓝[>] 0, and multiplication by the finite constant V(R)), stated for an arbitrary positive null sequence s and an arbitrary finite constant C.
1. (s tends to 0 from the right.) Since s_i → 0 and s_i ∈ (0, ∞) for every i, s tends to 0 within (0, ∞), i.e. s → 0 along 𝓝[>] 0 (tendsto_nhdsWithin_iff). Consequently, if a property Q(r) holds for all r in some member of 𝓝[>] 0, then Q(s_i) holds for all sufficiently large i.
2. (Pulling out the constant in (i).) Assume limsup_{r→0⁺} f(r) ≤ 1. Since C ≠ ∞, limsup_i C·f(s_i) = C·limsup_i f(s_i) (ENNReal.limsup_const_mul_of_ne_top, valid for every filter; ENNReal.limsup_const_mul would instead require a countable-intersection filter). Hence it suffices to show L := limsup_i f(s_i) ≤ 1, because then limsup_i C·f(s_i) = C·L ≤ C·1 = C (monotonicity of multiplication in [0,∞]).
3. (L ≤ 1.) Let c ∈ [0,∞] with c > 1. Then limsup_{r→0⁺} f(r) ≤ 1 < c, so f(r) < c for all r in some member of 𝓝[>] 0 (eventually_lt_of_limsup_lt; its boundedness side condition holds automatically in the complete lattice [0,∞]). By step 1, f(s_i) < c, hence f(s_i) ≤ c, for all sufficiently large i, and therefore L ≤ c (limsup_le_of_le). Since this holds for every c > 1 and [0,∞] is densely ordered, L ≤ 1 (le_of_forall_gt_imp_ge_of_dense). This proves (i).
4. (Part (ii).) Assume h(r) → 0 along 𝓝[>] 0. Composing with step 1 gives h(s_i) → 0 as i → ∞ (Tendsto.comp). Since C ≠ ∞, multiplication by the constant C preserves this limit in [0,∞] (ENNReal.Tendsto.const_mul, whose side condition 'limit ≠ 0 or C ≠ ∞' holds because C ≠ ∞), so C·h(s_i) → C·0 = 0. ∎
proof_key_steps: s_i > 0 and s_i → 0 give s → 0 along 𝓝[>] 0 (tendsto_nhdsWithin_iff).
For every c > 1, eventually f(s_i) < c, so limsup_i f(s_i) ≤ c; density of [0,∞] gives limsup_i f(s_i) ≤ 1, hence limsup_i C·f(s_i) ≤ C.
h(s_i) → 0 by composition, and C·h(s_i) → C·0 = 0 by ENNReal.Tendsto.const_mul since C ≠ ∞.

subproblems.title: Uniform bounds on compact sets for finite measures with eventually bounded ball masses
subproblems.statement: Let P ∈ ℕ and let ν_i (i ∈ ℕ) be measures on ℝ^P (= Euclid P) with ν_i(ℝ^P) < ∞ for every i. Assume that for every R > 0 there is B ∈ [0,∞] with B < ∞ such that ν_i(B̄_R(0)) ≤ B for all sufficiently large i (eventually along atTop). Then sup_i ν_i(K) < ∞ for every compact K ⊆ ℝ^P.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P : ℕ) (ν : ℕ → Measure (Euclid P)), (∀ i, ν i univ < ∞) → (∀ R : ℝ, 0 < R → ∃ B : ℝ≥0∞, B < ∞ ∧ ∀ᶠ i in atTop, ν i (closedBall 0 R) ≤ B) → ∀ K : Set (Euclid P), IsCompact K → ⨆ i, ν i K < ∞
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: step 4 (part (a)) of the parent proof. There the early indices are bounded by ν_i(K) ≤ c_i·Hⁿ(M), which equals ν_i(ℝ^P), and the late indices by ν_i(B̄_R(0)) ≤ 2V(R); here these two inputs are the two hypotheses.
1. (Enclosing ball.) K is compact, hence bounded, so K ⊆ B̄_{R₀}(0) for some R₀ ∈ ℝ (Bornology.IsBounded.subset_closedBall). Put R := max(R₀, 1). Then R ≥ 1 > 0 and K ⊆ B̄_{R₀}(0) ⊆ B̄_R(0).
2. (Late indices.) By the hypothesis applied to this R there are B < ∞ and N ∈ ℕ with ν_i(B̄_R(0)) ≤ B for all i ≥ N (eventually_atTop).
3. (Early indices.) Let S := Σ_{j=0}^{N−1} ν_j(ℝ^P). Each summand is finite by hypothesis, so S < ∞ (ENNReal.sum_lt_top).
4. (Pointwise bound.) Let i ∈ ℕ. If i ≥ N, then ν_i(K) ≤ ν_i(B̄_R(0)) ≤ B by monotonicity of ν_i and steps 1–2. If i < N, then ν_i(K) ≤ ν_i(ℝ^P) ≤ S by monotonicity of ν_i and because ν_i(ℝ^P) is one of the summands of S, all of which are ≥ 0 (Finset.single_le_sum with i ∈ {0, …, N−1}). In both cases ν_i(K) ≤ max(B, S).
5. (Conclusion.) Hence sup_i ν_i(K) ≤ max(B, S) (iSup_le), and max(B, S) < ∞ because B < ∞ and S < ∞ (max_lt). ∎
proof_key_steps: K compact ⇒ K ⊆ B̄_R(0) with R := max(R₀, 1) > 0.
The hypothesis gives B < ∞ and N with ν_i(B̄_R(0)) ≤ B for all i ≥ N.
For i < N, ν_i(K) ≤ ν_i(ℝ^P) ≤ Σ_{j<N} ν_j(ℝ^P) < ∞.
